experiment: Which law shapes can a derived generator actually refute?
design: Every stub in fixtures/verify-refutability is deliberately WRONG. Therefore any measured-bothPass is a FALSE NEGATIVE of the verifier, not a debatable result. No judgement call is needed to read the outcome.
hypothesis: CLAUDE.md: a property whose failure needs two generated values to COLLIDE is invisible to a generator drawing from a realistic domain. So: BROAD refuted, COLLISION survives, EDGE refuted iff the edge pass earns its keep.

scoring.REFUTED: verify reports defaultFails (or edgeCaseAdvisory naming the violation)

predictions.rationale: appends on every call; fails for every input
subtraction; fails for every a != b
decode drops a character; fails for every non-empty
tie-break only observable when two timestamps are EQUAL; the Decisions.merge shape, already measured as bothPass at 100 trials
needs two generated values in the same bucket (value % 8)
needs two generated intervals to be exactly adjacent
wrong only at Int.max; the verifier runs a dedicated edge pass and Int.max is the canonical integer edge
wrong only on the empty string; empty is the canonical String edge
wrong only at 0; zero is a canonical integer edge

result.coverage_rate: 6/44 = 14% of proposed laws produced ANY verdict

scored_predictions.note: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED on a purpose-built case: wrong only at multiples of 997, never drawn.
PREDICTION WRONG, and the reason is worse than the miss: the edge pass reported ZERO trials, so Int.min was never tried.

unpredicted.note: my union is BROADLY non-commutative (asymmetric drop), so this is a BROAD row, consistent with BROAD->refuted.

result.conclusion: Verification cannot substitute for precision TODAY, and the binding constraint is REACH rather than generator quality. 86% of proposed laws were never measured. Of the 14% that ran: the collision-dependent violation passed 100 trials while being false, and the edge-dependent one passed with the edge pass reporting zero trials.
